newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS and SAA to share routes.
newsitem.headline: SAS and SAA to share routes.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) and South African Airlines (SAA) are to begin joint flights between Denmark and South Africa from July 2, an SAS statement said on Tuesday.

It said that the alliance would begin on twice-weekly flights between Copenghagen, Johannesburg and Cape Town at first but would later expand to cover daily flights and more destinations. Both companies' codes would be retained, it added.
"Since 1985, when SAS had to end its route to South Africa, there has been no direct air connection between Scandinavia and the southern part of the African continent," the statement said.
It added that there was now strong Scandinavian business activity in the region and great potential for developing tourism.

"The new South African-SAS route will offer better and simpler flight connections between Scandinavia and South Africa. Co-operation will later expand to include connections to Oslo and Stockholm," the statement said.
When SAS, Lufthansa, United, Air Canada, Thai Airways International and Brazil's Varig launched their Star Alliance in May they said SAA was a potential future partner.
SAS is jointly owned by the governments of Denmark, Norway and Sweden and by private investors. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
